newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares drop 5.95pct in panic selling.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares drop 5.95pct in panic selling.

text.p: Greek shares plunged 5.95 percent on Thursday, after the capital market commission's warning against speculation on Wednesday created panic selling in the bourse, fund managers said.
On Wednesday, capital market commission president Stavros Thomadakis warned investors against speculation and rumour-based investment decisions.

"This warning was the occasion and not the real cause of the market drop. The reason behind this correction was the bourse's recent sharp rise and such a move was anticipated," said George Vendouratos, a fund manager at Aspis Mutual Funds.
However, the correction would probably have been smaller if the market had not reacted to the capital market commission's warning, he said.

"Instead of a 5.95 percent correction we could have seen a 3.0 percent correction on one day and another 3.0 percent on another day," he said, adding that he was not alarmed by the drop because the good fundamentals of the market have not changed.
Retail investors, who are usually the first to panic, were selling their shares on Thursday. But other investors who joined the selling wave were doing so to take profit during the session, he said.
"This is the time for selective buys. The market is in for a recovery," he added.
The Athens general share index closed 5.95 percent down or 86.44 points lower at 1367.16 points from Wednesday's 1453.60, after opening at 1448.80.
Turnover was 30.8 billion drachmas on volume of 6.9 million shares. Decliners led advancers 218 to 31 with 4 issues unchanged on 253 issues traded.
Sectoral indices were down, with biggest losses incurred in banking and construction shares, down 7.27 and 7.19 percent respectively.
Investment shares closed 6.17 percent lower and industrials settled 5.08 percent down.
Insurance stocks lost 3.99 percent and small caps ended weaker, down 3.22 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 993.00-1021.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, were trading 165 drachmas lower at 5,820.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 12,908-13,600 drachmas.
